steps.text: Preheat the oven 180ºC. Roll out the pastry to 4mm thick on a lightly floured surface. Cut out 10 11cm circles and 10 8cm circles of pastry. Use the larger circle to line a non stick mini muffin tin and chill. Chill the 8cm circles as these will be the lids.

Mix together 120 gm sugar (retain a little to sprinkle over later) the cinnamon the lemon juice and zest and stir gently into the pears and apples.
Place the pear and apple slices into the lined muffin tins. Cut the Flora Buttery into 10 and dot each pie with butter and sprinkle with chopped rosemary.
Place the smaller circles on top of the sliced pears and apples. Seal the edges well. Make a small hole in the top to allow steam to escape.
Egg wash with lightly beaten egg and sprinkle with the remaining sugar.
Bake at 180°c for 30 mins until the fruit is tender and the top is golden brown.

steps.text: Combining the sugar wine vinegar and soy sauce. Add this to the beef and set aside to marinate for a minimum of 2 hours ideally over night.
Peel and dice the onions into 1cm dice. Peel and very finely mince the ginger and garlic. Deseed and cut the peppers into 1cm dice. Half de-seed and very finely slice the chilli.

Place a suitable size pan over a medium heat add half of the rapeseed oil along with the onions ginger garlic and chilli. Fry for 5-10 minutes or until the onions begin to soften and it smells aromatic. At this point add the black bean sauce to the pan bring to the boil remove from the heat and set aside to rest.

steps.text: Preheat the oven 170ºC. Grease a 26cm x 32cm x 5cm brownie tin. Scrape the seeds from the vanilla pod.

To make the frosting place the cream cheese margarine and icing sugar into the bowl of a food mixer and Whisk together until smooth and thickened. Melt the dark chocolate and whisk into the mixture.
Spread the mixture over the cooled blondie and cut into 10.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 150ºC. Preheat the deep fryer to 180ºC. Dilute the bouillon with the water. Dust the short rib in 3/4 of the flour and in a suitable pan heat the oil and brown the short rib on all side until golden brown. Peel and cut the carrot celery and onion into even sizes. Once the short ribs are brown remove from the pan and drain 50% of the rendered fat add the chopped vegetables and brown on all sides.
Return the short rib to the pan add the stout thyme bay leaf and beef stock bring to a gentle simmer.
Tightly foil the saucepan and place in the preheated oven for 4 hours or until tender.
Carefully remove pan from the oven and allow the rib to cool in the braising liquor.
Once cool enough to handle remove the short rib pass the liquor and reduce by half. Meanwhile trim the short rib of any excess fat and portion into 10 equal portions.

Return the short rib to the reduce liquor and heat through season with the pepper. Peel and finely slice the shallots into rings and dust in the remaining flour carefully place into a preheated fryer 180ºC until golden. Drain. Serve short rib with reduce liquored and top with fried shallots.

steps.text: Peel and dice the butternut squash and apple 1 cm dice. Peel and finely dice the onions celery garlic and ginger. Wash the red lentils.

Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion celery garlic and ginger. Cook stirring occasionally for 5 minutes or until the onion is soft and a light brown in colour add the cumin and coriander.
Next add the squash and apples to the pot. Saute for a minute or two. Mix in the lentils pour in the water. Bring mixture to a boil season and taste.

Reduce heat to low cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes or until the lentils have melted into the soup and the squash and apples are tender. Remove half the mix and puree. Add the puree back into the soup.
Taste the soup and adjust seasoning if needed. For the maple seeds
Preheat an oven to 200oC. Mix the seeds maple syrup and salt together. Scatter onto a baking tray and bake 8-10 minute. Until golden. Remove and allow to cool.
Serve the soup with a topping of the maple seeds.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Line a couple baking trays with parchment paper.

PREP; Peel half and scoop out the seeds of the butternut squash. Slice into 0.5cm pieces. Finely slice the leeks wash and thoroughly drain. Grate the gruyere cheese. Finely slice the sage leaves. Whisk together 1 egg + 1 egg yolk. Pick thyme leaves.

In a bowl add the butternut nut squash oil picked thyme salt and freshly cracked pepper. Toss to coat and transfer to the lined baking tray. Roast for 10-15 minutes or till just tender. Remove from heat and chill.

In a Saucepan on medium heat add oil. Once hot add the leeks and sauté for 3-4 minutes or till softened. Add the sage salt and freshly cracked pepper and cook for a further 1 minute. Remove from heat and chill.
Defrost the puff pastry sheets and cut out 20 rounds in 15cm diameter (roughly the size of a small side plate). Place half the rounds on a lined baking sheet.

Sprinkle the centre of each pastry circle with a little grated gruyere. Layer slices of the squash leek and grated gruyere seasoning as you go. Keep layering till you have a dome shape about 5cm high. MAKE SURE YOU LEAVE A 2cm EDGE AROUND THE OUTSIDE. Egg was the edge and then drape another puff pastry round on top and press edge with a fork to seal it tight. Brush the pastry tops with beaten egg and mark a spiral or criss-cross pattern lightly into the pastry top.

steps.text: Very finely mince the garlic.

Place the pancetta and rapeseed into a suitable size cold pan and place over a medium heat. Slowly fry the pancetta releasing all the fat and cook until its golden and crispy. Remove using a slotted spoon retaining the fat in the pan.
Add the garlic to the rendered fat and gently fry until soft and translucent return the pancetta to the pan remove from the heat and set aside.

Place a portion of the rendered pancetta into a clean small sauce pan along with some of the garlic and reserved fat. Re-heat a portion of the pasta in rolling boiling water for 20 seconds add this to the pancetta portion along with 2-3 tbsp. of the pasta water. Remove from the heat then add the egg yolk and the grated pecorino. Working quickly combine the ingredients together. steps.text: Steam the condensed milk for 3 hours then allow to cool completely before opening. Best to do this the day before.

Use a electric mixer with a paddle attachment. Mix together the eggs sugar vanilla extract 75g melted butter and milk. Puree the bananas smashing it with a fork and add it to the mix. In a separate bowl mix the sift the flour baking powder bicarbonate of soda salt cinnamon and nutmeg together.
Fold in the dry ingredients to the banana mix until it is a lumpy paste.

Set paper cases into the moulds or grease the moulds well with butter and pipe in the mixture until almost full. Pipe a dollop of the pre cooked toffee right in the middle of the uncooked muffins and cover it completely with a little extra muffin mix.
For the crumble: Mix all together with the paddle attachment until a sand texture.
Sprinkle the crumble mix on top of the muffins and bake at 180C for 20 to 25 minutes.
Rest the muffin tray on a wire rack for five minutes then remove the muffins and leave on the rack for another five minutes before serving.

steps.text: Place a large pan of salted water on a high heat.

FOR THE BARLEY COUSCOUS; Place the couscous in a gastro tray season with salt drizzle with 30ml olive oil then rub the grains between your hands to coat the couscous and distribute the oil evenly. Pour over the boiling water just enough to cover the couscous then cover with a lid. Leave for 5 minutes. Take the lid off and use a fork to break up the couscous into individual grains and set aside to cool.

FOR THE BULGAR WHEAT; Place the bulgar in a gastro tray season with salt drizzle with 30ml olive oil then rub the grains between your hands to coat the bulgar and distribute the oil evenly. Pour over the boiling water covering the grains with about 2-3cm of the water then cover with a lid. Leave for 20 minutes. Take the lid off and use a fork to fluff up the bulgar into individual grains and set aside to cool.
Mix the barley couscous and bulgar together. NOTE: COUSCOUS typically takes equal parts water to couscous. The BULGAR WHEAT typically takes 1.5parts water to 1 part grain.

FOR THE PUY LENTILS; Rinse the lentils for 20 seconds. Then add to a medium sized pot with 3x their volume of water (1 part grain to 3 parts water). Bring to the boil and boil for 30 seconds then turn heat down to a low simmer and cover. Cook for 22-25 minutes or till the lentils are. Season with salt and freshly cracked pepper to taste then put the lid back on. Leave the lentils to sit for 5 minutes then drain and cool.
Mix the basmati and lentils together.

steps.text: Crack the egg yolks into a bowl add the cream finely grate in the Parmigiano Reggiano and season with freshly cracked black pepper then mix well.

Dice the pancetta into 1cm removing the rind. Add the pancetta to a large frying pan and sauté over medium-low heat until browned and crisp around 5 minutes. Cook the tagliatelle in a large pan of generously salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes or until al dente (taste a piece before removing from the water).

Finish with freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano and a healthy grind of black pepper.

Cook rice and let cook

Place a large scoop on to the wrap and fold tight
Slice in half at an angle.

title: Indian Spiced Cauliflower  Romanesco and Apple

ingredients.text: 50 ML Oil Rapeseed Extended Life KTC

steps.text: .Prepare the cauliflower and Romanesco into small florets. Peel and dice apple 1 cm dice. Peel and finely dice the onions and celery peel and finely grate the garlic and ginger. Deseed and finely chop chilli. 2.Keep 500g of cauliflower and Romanesco back and 200g apple for the raita. 3.Heat 30ml oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion celery garlic and ginger. Cook stirring occasionally for 5 minutes or until the onion is soft and a light brown in colour. Next add the cauliflower Romanesco and chilli to the pot. Sauté for 3-4 mins then add the cumin turmeric curry powder and ground coriander. Cook out for 1 2mins.

Mix in the apples pour in the water. Bring mixture to a boil season and taste. 5.Reduce to a low heat cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes or until the cauliflower and apples are tender. Puree the soup in a blender or with a stick blender. Taste the soup and adjust seasoning if needed. Set aside. For the Raita Mix.

Heat 20ml oil in a pan sauté the remaining Romanesco/cauliflower for a few minutes and nearly cooked add the diced apple zest and juice of lemon. Season with Maldon salt cook for a further minute. Remove from heat and allow to cool. Add the yoghurt to the mix with finely chopped coriander.
Serve the soup hot with a topping of the raita.

title: Indian Style Scramble Eggs With Naan & Tomato

ingredients.text: 1.5 L Egg Whole Free Range Liquid

steps.text: PREP; Mix the liquid egg double cream salt and pepper together. Peel half and finely dice the onion. Finely chop the tomatoes. Finely slice the green chilli. Grate the garlic and ginger. Pick the leaves off the coriander then roughly chop the leaves and finely cut the stalks keep separate. Defrost the naan bread.

FOR THE SPICE PASTE; In a non-stick pan on medium-high heat the oil. Add onions and stir until softened. Add tomatoes cook until most of the excess moisture has evaporated. Add green chilli ginger garlic coriander STALKS and stir until fragrant. Add chilli powder garam masala and turmeric powder and stir until oil separates from the paste taking care not to burn the paste. Remove from heat. (NOTE; Spice paste can be made the day before and stored in fridge.)
Warm the naan bread in the steamer or hot box.
In a large shallow saucepan on medium heat add the oil and spice paste stir and then add the egg mix stirring gently with a rubber spatula. When the eggs are just about done take off the heat.

TO SERVE; Transfer a portion of eggs to desired 12oz disposable breakfast pot. Top with a heaped tbsp of tomato chutney and a naan bread to the side of the eggs. Sprinkle the roughly chopped coriander leaves over top.

steps.text: Soak the skewers overnight. Preheat the oven 180ºC. Remove any skin bone and fat from the chicken thigh and cut into even size chunks.
Mix together the sherry soy mirin and sugar in a pan place on the stove and reduce the mix to a syrup.

Blend the chicken in a blender. Mix the chicken with the eggs plain flour cornflour breadcrumbs salt and pepper together to form a paste. Leave in the fridge for 1 hour then form into 40 equal size balls (per 10 portions).
Peel and cut the ginger into large chunks and place into a pan of boiling water (larger enough to poach the chicken balls).
Cook the balls in the ginger water for approx 10 minutes and then chill the balls.
Roll the cooled balls in the cooled syrup thread 4 balls onto each skewer chill until require.
Griddle each skewer until core temperature is reached (75ºC ENG 82ºC SCOT).
Serve.

steps.text: Make the raita as per sub recipe. Peel and slice the onions finely chop the coriander deseed and dice the chillies peel and mince the ginger and garlic.
Wash the rice and leave to soak for about for 20-30 minutes.

Heat the oil in a pan and add the cumin seeds cook for a minute. Add the coriander seeds peppercorns cardamom fennel seeds cloves and cook for 30 seconds. Add the sliced onions and sweat down for around 5 minutes.
Add the ginger garlic and chillies and cook for a minute.
Add the lamb mince to the pan in small chunks and cook for 5-6 minutes over a medium heat until the lamb is 70% cooked.
Strain the mince to remove the fat and return to the pan. Add the drained rice to the pan and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add the water garam masala cumin seeds and salt to the pan and put on a medium to high heat mixing occasionally.

Once the water had almost disappeared add the coriander to the pan. Cover with 2 layers of foil lower the heat and cook for 2 minutes before removing from the heat. Leave covered for 15-20 minutes before removing the foil and opening up the rice using a wooden spoon to gently lift and shake the rice.
Garnish as desired and serve with the raita.

steps.text: Combine flour and oil in a bowl. Slowly add the water and bring together for a soft dough. Need for 5-15 minutes either by hand or in a mixer until a smooth dough is achieved.
Place dough into a lightly oiled bowl and cover before leaving for 15-20 minutes to rest or place in the fridge until needed.
When ready to make the Parathas put a dry frying pan over a medium heat.
Split the dough evenly into 10 pieces roll each piece into a ball. Cover the balls so that they dont dry out. Melt the butter in a pan.

Flatten a ball of dough using your fingers before lightly dusting in flour and rolling out to a diameter of approximately 12cm. Brush with butter and sprinkle with salt before rolling the dough into a long sausage to close up the disc. Even the sausage out using your palms before taking one side of the dough and curling it into a spiral. Tuck the end piece into the middle and press down until fixed into place.

Lightly dust both sides with flour and roll out once again this time to a diameter of approx. 20cm. Brush the excess flour off from the disc. Turn the heat up on the pan slightly and place the bread into the pan. Let the bread cook for 45 seconds on one side before flipping over and cooking for 35 seconds on the other side. Brush the bread with a little more butter and turn over cook for a further 30 seconds before brushing the other side with butter and flipping over and cooking the bread until golden brown slightly crispy and cooked through.

steps.text: Peel and mince the ginger and garlic. Deseed and mince the chillies and combine with the ginger and garlic. Finely chop the coriander.

Make the kofta balls by mixing the lamb mince with half of the minced ginger garlic and chilli and half of the chopped coriander. Add the ground coriander half of the turmeric half of the chilli powder and half of the ground cumin. Mix thoroughly and season to taste. Divide the mix into 30 balls (3 balls per portion). Place balls into the fridge.

Hard boil and peel the eggs. Peel and finely dice the onions. Blend the plum tomatoes until smooth. To make the masala sauce heat the oil over a medium heat and add the cumin seeds to cook for about a minute. Add the onions and cook for about 10 minutes until the onions are golden brown.
Once the onions are brown add the remaining ginger garlic and chilli to the pan and cook for a couple of minutes.
Add the blended tomatoes to the pan and cook for 5 minutes before blitzing using a hand blender. Add the remaining turmeric chilli powder ground cumin and butter to the sauce and cook for
20 minutes adding a little more water if the sauce starts to stick to the bottom of the pan.

Once the sauce is thick and has become a darker orange colour add the water so the sauce becomes a curry consistency cook for about 2 mins before adding the koftas to the curry and cooking on a medium heat for about 15-20 mins.

Cook the potatoes in the deep-fat fryer for approx. 10 minutes or until softened. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside to drain on kitchen paper. Turn the deep fryer up to 190ºC.

When ready to serve. With a slotted spoon lower all the par-cooked chips gently into the fryer and cook for 4-5 minutes or until crisp and golden-brown. Remove from the pan with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Season with the salt and keep warm while you cook the steak.

Drain the meat reserving the marinade. Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until just smoking and add the meat to the wok be careful it might splutter at you. Cook as quickly as possible tossing it until the meat is browned on all sides.
Add the red onion wedges and cook for one minute. Add the tomato and chilli.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180*C.
FOR THE GLAZE; In a saucepan add the honey zest and juice of the orange crushed cinnamon stick crushed garlic cloves and picked thyme leaves. Reduce the sauce by half.

Pat dry the duck breast with blue kitchen paper. Lightly score the fat with a sharp knife. Season with salt and leave for 10 minutes. Pat dry again and in a dry frying pan skin side down. Turn the heat up to medium low temperature and cook for 6-8 minutes or till the skin is crisp and golden. Pour off any excess fat as you cook*. Flip the breast over and seal the meat for 30 seconds. Transfer the duck breast to an oven tray skin side up and roast for 5-7 minutes or till core temp is 54*C brush duck with the orange glaze twice.
Remove duck from the oven brush one more time with the orange glaze and leave to rest on a wire rack for 5 minutes.
Slice and serve with roasted vegetables savoy cabbage and mulled cherry sauce.

title: Pastel de Tres Leches (Three Milk Cake)

ingredients.text: 600 ML Milk Whole Pasteurised Standard RT

steps.text: Separate the egg yolks and whites. Heat the oven to 180ºC. Melt the butter. Line a gastro try with greaseproof paper. In an electric mixer fitted with the whisk attachment combine egg whites baking powder and salt and beat on medium speed until soft peaks form 2-3 minutes.
Add yolks to the whites and beat until completely combined. With the mixer running slowly add sugar until combined. Remove the bowl from the mixer. Using a rubber spatula fold in melted butter.

Sift 40g (per 10 portions) flour on top of the mixture and fold in to combine. Repeat with the remaining flour folding in 40g at a time. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake until golden and a cake tester inserted into the middle comes out clean 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven and transfer to a wire rack.

About 5 minutes before the cake is done whisk together the three milks and set aside. As soon as the cake is removed from the oven pour the milk mixture over the entire cake. The cake should absorb all the liquid within 3-5 minutes. Set cake aside and let stand until cool. Cover cake well and transfer to the refrigerator to chill at least 5 hours or overnight.
Lightly toast coconut shavings.
When ready to serve the cake whip cream to soft peaks spread over cake cover toasted coconut and cut to desired size.

Put the butter sugar eggs flour and vanilla in a food processor and pulse until well combined.
Transfer the batter into 6 bowls equally split

Leave in fridge for 1 hour then slice to desired thickness.

steps.text: First make the craquelin. It needs to be frozen when placed on top of the choux past to bake.
In a kitchen aid with the paddle attachment mix demerara sugar 30g butter and 30g flour. Mix until it become a paste.
Place this paste in between two silicone matts and with a rolling pin make it flat with about 0.5cm of thickness. Freeze it.
To make the choux paste: In a large pot place water milk 125g butter and the 12g sugar together. Bring it to the boil.
Away from the heat add sieved flour and salt mix it well and cook it as a roux base.
Place the still hot mix into a kitchen aid with a paddle attachment and mix in low speed.
As it mix add eggs one by one turn speed to medium until the paste come together.
Pipe the choux paste into a lined baking tray into blobs of 20g each.
Cut the frozen craquelin into discs to cover the choux place it on top and bake it at 200*c for 15 minutes.
Open the oven to let the steam out and bake it at 180*c for another 10 min.
Once the buns are cold you can fill them with your flavour of choice. Ganaches pastry cream fruit compotes. Anything you fancy.

steps.text: Preheat the oven 180ºC. For the pastry: Cream together 3 eggs and 125 gm sugar add the 300 gm Flora Buttery and mix together gradually add the flour and salt until smooth and leave to rest for 1 hour.

Roll out the pastry to 4mm thick on a lightly floured surface. Cut out 10 11cm circles and 10 8cm circles of pastry. Use the larger circle to line a non stick mini muffin tin and chill. Chill the 8cm circles as these will be the lids.

For the filling: Peel quarter and core the pears slice thickly into a bowl with the lemon juice and stir in the honey and scraped vanilla. Combine the brown sugar walnuts and cornflour in another bowl. Stir pear mixture into sugar mixture. Spoon the pear mixture into the lined muffin tin. Cut the remaining Flora Buttery into 10 and dot each pie with butter.
Place the smaller circles on top of the filled pies. Seal the edges well. Make a small hole in the top to allow steam to escape.
Egg wash with lightly beaten egg and sprinkle with the remaining sugar.
Bake at 180°c for 30 mins until the fruit is tender and the top is golden brown.

steps.text: Preheat the oven 180ºC. Roll out the pastry to 4mm thick on a lightly floured surface. Cut out 10 11cm circles and 10 8cm circles of pastry. Use the larger circle to line a non stick mini muffin tin and chill. Chill the 8cm circles as these will be the lids.

For the filling: Trim the rhubarb and cut into short lengths zest and juice the orange. Place rhubarb caster sugar (retain a little to sprinkle over later) orange juice and zest ginger and cornflour in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook stirring for 4 to 5 minutes or until mixture has thickened and heated through. Cool.
Place the rhubarb mix into the lined muffin tins. Cut the butter into 10 and dot each pie with Flora Buttery..
Place the smaller circles on top of the filled pies. Seal the edges well. Make a small hole in the top to allow steam to escape.
Egg wash with lightly beaten egg and sprinkle with the remaining sugar.
Bake at 180°c for 30 mins until the fruit is tender and the top is golden brown.

steps.text: Peel and finely dice the onion. Very finely slice the garlic. Halve the chilli lengthways and finely slice (disguard the seeds). Dissolve the bouillon in the water.
Add the rapeseed to a suitable size saucepan and place over a low-medium heat. Add the garlic to the pan and gently fry until it begins to just caramelise.

Add the onions and chilli to the garlic and continue to cook for a further 3-5 minutes. Add the tomato puree and cook for a further 3-5 minutes until just starting to caramelise. Add the Passata vegetable stock and then caster sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for a further 30minutes until slightly reduced and concentrated in flavour. Add the dried chilli flakes and set aside.

Re-heat a portion of the pasta in rolling boiling water for 20 seconds remove and dress with a portion of the finished sauce (adding a little water if required to achieve the right consistency). Serve as required finished with the olive oil and freshly grated pecorino (to order).

steps.text: Peel Onions & Garlic. Roughly dice onion in 1cm pieces dont chop the garlic but crush the whole cloves with the flat part of your knife.
Dice pork joint into 2-3cm pieces. (1400gm for 10 portions reserve in extra for additional recipes). Heat a large heavy based saucepan on a high heat & add the oil.
Add the diced pork piece by piece to the hot oil (This is to help maintain as much heat in the pan as possible. Do this in smaller batches if you are doing multiple portions).

Brown this pork very well on all sides (try not to stir to much as this will make it sweat) Once Browned remove from the pan & set aside. Keep the pan on the heat but reduce the temperature. Add the diced onion crushed garlic bay leaves & thyme.
Sweat these for 4-5 minutes until soft. Once soft add the tomato puree oregano & smoked paprika. Cook this for 1-2 minutes.

Add the red wine & de glaze the pan Reduce this wine by half. Return pork to the pan along with the passata water & bouillon. Stir well & cover with a cartouche or lid. Reduce temperature to a slow simmer & cook for between 1 & half hours to 2 hours until the pork is tender.
Remove lid & add honey & vinegar. Serve immediately.

Again keeping the same pan on the heat add the diced onion garlic bay leaves & un-chopped thyme. For the caramel place the remaining sugar and water in pan place on a medium heat bring to the boil for around 12 mins until the sugar has a deep dark brown color remove from the heat and carefully add the butter and cream whisk to combine all once the butter has melted pout over the cooled shortbread and set in the fridge.

steps.text: Pre heat Oven to 180 deg.

Place flour 240gm of castor sugar ground star Anise and salt in a bowl make a well in the middle add 200gm of the pineapple puree sunflower oil the egg yolks (keep the whites for later) orange zest and vanilla seeds whisk all together to form a batter.

Pour the mix into a non-greased chiffon cake tin not more the 3/4 cm from the top bake for 50 mins check with a skewer invert the cake tin it wont fall as its not greased allow to cool.

steps.text: Start by soaking all the seeds in 175ml of boiled water overnight the following morning start by mixing all the ingredients together in a large bowl tip onto a lightly oiled surface use the heel of your hand push away the dough and then pull back repeat this stretching and tearing technique to build up the gluten for approx. 10 mins. Place in clean lightly bowl and cling film keep in a warm environment for

4 hours Knock back the dough by folding it building up more gluten at least 4 times. Prove the dough till its double in size shape the dough into a tight ball for the final shape flatten into a square shape then fold in the corners and form into an oval shape seam side down lightly flour the top and place into a proving basket prove at room temp for another 2 hours score the dough before baking at 230 deg for 25 mins then check add some ice cubes to the oven and bake for a further 25 mins the loaf should dark in color and hollow sound when tapped allow to cool completely before slicing.

steps.text: Method: Fry the croquettes at 170/180*c and finished in the oven at 170*c for 1 min or till the reach 75*c. Truffle Aioli: Place the garlic cloves the flat parsley leaves the vinegar the salt the mustard and the milk into a large container and with the help of a hand blender blitz while pouring slowly the Olive oil into the mixture. Without stopping continue pouring the vegetable oil slowly but constantly so the oil emulsifies with the liquid mixture. It will get thicker and thicker as we add the oil. At the end finish it with the truffle oil. We need to judge ourselves when the consistency is right as some times it accepts more oil than others depending on the weather temperature blender speed... The texture should be silky and smooth and the consistency should not be runny quite stable but not as hard as a fake mayonnaise. Always taste it when finished if you are not sure give it to taste to the chef in charge.

Place the aubergines on a platter over lapping cover evenly with the yoghurt and then sprinkle over the drained lemon pickle.
Dress with chopped pistachios and chopped chervil.

steps.text: Defrost the spinach in the fridge overnight (best to do this in a colander or chinois to drain the water).
Preheat the oven to 190*C. Line trays with greaseproof paper. Bake the sweet potatoes in the oven for approx. 90 minutes or until tender leave to cool. Once cool to touch peel and mash.

Chop the rosemary. Crumble the goats cheese. Zest the lemon. Remove crusts & blend the bread to a crumb. Squeeze any excess water out of the spinach and roughly chop. Beat the eggs together. Mince the garlic then add to the melted butter to infuse a little.

For the balls; mix together the mashed sweet potato bread crumbs lemon zest spinach melted garlic butter 150g panko goats cheese rosemary salt pepper & mix together. Chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.

Combine the parmesan and remaining 50g panko together. Divide the mixture into 30 x 50g balls roll the balls through the breadcrumb mix and place onto the baking tray and cook in the oven for approx. 20 minutes (turning whilst cooking) or until nicely browned and the core temperature has reached 75 *C.
Serve the balls with the curry sauce brown rice chilli slaw and garnish with the picked coriander and crispy onions.

steps.text: First prepare the corn on the cob by removing from the husk and cutting the corn off from the cob then set aside. Peel and dice the apple. Then peel and dice the onions potato and celery. Finally peel and grate the garlic pick the thyme leaves and chop.

Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and celery cook stirring occasionally for 5 minutes or until the onion is a soft and light brown colour. Next add the sweetcorn garlic thyme and potato to the pot. Sauté for 3-4 mins then add the apple cook out for 1 2mins.

Pour in the water. Bring mixture to a boil season with 6g salt white pepper and taste. 4.Reduce to a low heat cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until the vegetables and apples are tender. Puree the soup in a blender or with a stick blender. Taste the soup again and adjust the seasoning if needed. Set aside. For the crème fraiche salsa.

Peel and finely chop the spring onions deseed the green chilli and finely chop also finely chop the parsley. Zest and juice the lemon. Add all to the crème fraiche with the remaining salt and mix well.
Serve the soup hot with a topping of the salsa.

With a sharp knife score the fat of each duck breast in a criss- cross pattern then sprinkle over half the five-spice powder salt and rub in.

Turn the duck breasts over and cook for a further 30 seconds to seal the other side. Place the pan in the oven for the duck to finish cooking (8 minutes for rare or 10 minutes for medium rare) then remove the duck and leave to rest on a chopping board for 10 minutes.
Pour any excess duck fat from the pan into a bowl.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in a large pan of rolling boiling water according to manufactures instructions - cook to al dente. Drain well and refresh under cold running water until cool.

Add oil & butter to a pan on a low medium heat & toast breadcrumbs for 3-4 minutes. Add garlic & thyme & stir over heat for a further 2 minutes or until the crumb is crisp & golden brown. Remove from the pan to a mixing bowl & allow to cool.

To make cheese sauce - Place milk cream cloves onion & bay leaf into a pan & bring to a simmer slowly. In another pan melt butter & add flour to create a roux. Cook out the flour on a medium heat for a few minutes. Pass milk through a sieve to remove cloves & bay leaf. Whisk the milk slowly into the roux mix until smooth.
Add salt remaining cheese mustard & white pepper. Whisk gently until cheese has melted. Mix cheese sauce & pasta together.
Portion into correct service dish (individual portions) top with more Cheese.
Cook in preheated oven 170*c for approx. 25-30 minutes. Ensure the core temperature reaches 75c ENG (82c SCOT).
Serve on correct service plate with salad and garlic bread.

In another pan melt butter & add flour to create a roux. Cook out the flour on a medium heat for a few minutes. Pass milk through a sieve to remove cloves & bay leaf. Whisk the milk slowly into the roux mix until smooth. 4. Add salt remaining cheese mustard & white pepper. Whisk gently until cheese has melted. Mix cheese sauce & pasta together. 5. Portion into correct service dish (individual portions) top with more Cheese. 6. Cook in preheated oven 170*c for approx. 25-30 minutes. Ensure the core temperature reaches 75c ENG (82c SCOT). 7. Serve on correct service plate with salad and garlic bread.
